readings: Linking lab records to patients by `ID` (dropping unmatched lab records), first average each patient's (`ID`, `SEX`) `ALB` and their per-test ratio of `UN` to `T-BIL`. Then, for each sex (leaving out patients whose `SEX` is blank or missing), average those patient-level figures. Which sexes have an average `ALB` above the mean of the sex-level `ALB` averages? Show the sex, its average `ALB`, its average `UN`/`T-BIL` ratio, and how far its `ALB` average is above that mean. Averages ignore missing values (including ratios that can't be computed); don't round.
queries:
WITH patient_level AS (
    SELECT P.ID, P.SEX,
           AVG(L.ALB) AS avg_alb,
           AVG(CASE WHEN L."T-BIL" IS NOT NULL AND L."T-BIL" <> 0 THEN CAST(L.UN AS REAL) / L."T-BIL" END) AS avg_ratio
    FROM Laboratory L
    JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID
    WHERE P.SEX IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(P.SEX) <> ''
    GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX
),
sex_level AS (
    SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_alb) AS avg_alb, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_ratio
    FROM patient_level
    GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT SEX, avg_alb, avg_ratio,
       avg_alb - (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) FROM sex_level) AS alb_above_mean
FROM sex_level
WHERE avg_alb > (SELECT AVG(avg_alb) FROM sex_level);
